contracts.commit_point: conn.execute(guardrail_result.sql) inside the connection block of run_sql_query (backend/app/genai/query_executor.py:47).
contracts.declared_mechanism: run_sql_query invokes validate_query(sql) at query_executor.py:43 before execution. validate_query (sql_guardrails.py:121-149) rejects empty input (123-124), normalizes the text by stripping comments and collapsing whitespace (48-63), enforces a single statement via _ensure_single_statement (66-71), enforces SELECT-only start and blocks FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS on literal-stripped text via _ensure_read_only (74-84, keyword list at 10-24), extracts FROM/JOIN table references via _extract_tables (87-91), rejects empty or non-whitelisted table sets via _ensure_only_allowed_tables using get_allowed_tables (94-102, 131-138), and injects or clamps LIMIT to settings.AI_SQL_MAX_LIMIT via _apply_or_clamp_limit (105-118, 140-143). Only the sanitized guardrail_result.sql is executed (query_executor.py:47) and returned (query_executor.py:56). On rejection, the agent tool converts ValueError/QueryExecutionError into ModelRetry so the model must correct the SQL (client.py:78-82).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Reaching conn.execute against the analytics database with SQL that has not passed validate_query: a multi-statement query; a statement that does not start with SELECT or contains any FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS token (insert, update, delete, drop, alter, truncate, attach, detach, replace, create, pragma, vacuum, reindex); a query with no explicit FROM/JOIN table or a table outside get_allowed_tables(); or a query whose LIMIT is absent or above settings.AI_SQL_MAX_LIMIT.

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of agent-tool-supplied SQL against the analytics SQLite database opened by _get_connection() inside run_sql_query.
contracts.protected_resource: The analytics SQLite database file resolved by get_analytics_db_path(), accessed via sqlite3.connect in _get_connection (backend/app/genai/query_executor.py:24-33).
contracts.protection_obligation: SQL supplied to the agent's execute_sql tool must pass validate_query guardrail validation — a single read-only SELECT statement free of write/DDL/PRAGMA forbidden keywords, referencing only explicitly named FROM/JOIN tables from the allowed analytics whitelist, with a LIMIT injected or clamped to settings.AI_SQL_MAX_LIMIT — before it is executed against the analytics SQLite database. (Merged from both reviewers, who describe the same obligation with identical guard, commit point, and effect path.)
scope_limits: Covers only the execute_sql -> run_sql_query -> validate_query path present in the supplied views; repository enumeration is incomplete, so no claim is made that no other code path executes SQL against the analytics database.

No claim about runtime efficacy or bypass-resistance of the regex-based checks (comment stripping, keyword matching, FROM/JOIN table extraction, LIMIT regex); the contract asserts only that these checks are declared and invoked before the commit point.

The connection is opened with plain sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5) with no read-only mode shown (query_executor.py:31); read-only enforcement rests entirely on validate_query, not on connection-level restrictions.
AnalystResult.validate_sql (client.py:35-44) is an output-field check on the final structured result, not part of the pre-execution guard, and is not relied upon by this contract.

The HTTP layer (routers/ai.py, ai_service, /ai/query endpoint) referenced in reviewer rationale is not present in supplied sources and is not asserted here; ordinary web authentication/CORS and generic application validation remain out of scope.
